posts.author: Roosterwiesel
posts.body:
Hi everyone,
I recently started working on some character designs for my project. When I began, I
assumed that 48x48 was the standard size
, so I designed a few characters without really using a strict 48x48 grid while drawing them.
Now that I’m trying to actually fit them into the
48x48 format
, I’ve realized that some of my designs probably
don’t translate very well to that size
. A lot of the details become hard to read or just don’t fit properly anymore.
Since I’m still pretty new to this, I’m not really sure what the best approach is.
Do you have any suggestions on
how I could adapt these designs so they work better in 48x48
?
Would it be better to simplify the designs, redraw them directly on a 48x48 grid, or maybe approach the sprites in a different way?
Any advice would be really appreciated!
Thanks!

posts.author: Midona018
posts.body:
You don't have to make them fit a 48x48 grid. RPG Maker supports all character sizes, but they have to fit the default format : all the images are the same size, and the placement of the images must be the same as the default one.
The only problem would be the relative size of the tiles, but the tileset can be adapted.

standard only means that most sprites use that, it does not mean that it is required or that the engine in any way cares about it.
any sprite size will work in the engine as long as it is done correctly, from 16x16 to 500x280 and so on.
some sprites might get too big to fit on the screen, but that does not mean that they would not work.
you on the other hand seem to have assumed that the 48x48 is forced on the sprites, and that is not correct.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
They are the standard and size of most default sprites (aside from the 'big monsters'), but that is exactly why some people don't like to use them.
Because using 48x48 makes the actors look "chibi", and a lot of people prefer using taller 72x48 or 96x48 sprites.
and your original picture example in the first post is a tall character (even if too many pixels to fit in regularly, so you can't use 48x48 for that, a 96x48 would be much better

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
cockwiesel said:
But If I would stick to 72x48 I would probably also have to resize the other assets in the game or am I wrong here?
Click to expand...
no, you should NEVER resize pixel art because it will always result in quality loss.
and reducing size is always an additional quality loss because you are removing pixel information.
you need to make the sprite at 72x48 in the first place, you never make a larger sprite to resize it to smaller.
but yes, as long as you keep to the restrictions as stated in the tutorial I linked above (and its answer posts when other people asked), then you can mix any size of sprite in the game.
